desc: Apply the existing D48 process isolation and cleanup contract to C6's three exit-release A9 oracle consumers (slice finding F1): TestOracleA9HaltRelease, TestOracleA9BlockReleasedStale and TestOracleA9BlockDoerStale. Remove their parallel overlap and wire the existing supervisor ownership helpers into their launches and cleanup. Add focused controlled failure/cancellation coverage. Preserve production behavior, all oracle assertions, fixtures and goldens. Run touched-file pre-commit before submission and record commands, tested SHA, outcomes and the unchanged fixture/golden diff.
done_when: All three named tests run serially, establish the existing D48 ownership before supervisor launch and clean up on success, cancellation, deadline and assertion failure. On Linux, direct supervisors are waited before remaining actual children, including adopted zombies, are reaped with bounded waits and an empty-child assertion. Other hosts retain D45 best-effort process-group cleanup and applicable existing skips. A focused held-provider failure/cancellation regression proves the exit-release consumers use cleanup; existing adopted-zombie coverage is reused where it exercises the same helper. Halt release, stale-owner state effects, prompt-spacing barrier, fixtures, goldens and existing assertions are unchanged. No new process-tracking mechanism. The focused C6 oracle/cleanup tests, A9 package and package-filtered provenance check pass under env -i. Evidence distinguishes historical results from new executions.
scope: Only internal/oracle/a9/exit_release_test.go, new C6-specific cleanup regression files under internal/oracle/a9 if needed, and C6 correction evidence. Reuse existing D48 helpers without editing the shared helpers or generic kit runners; this makes the write set disjoint from integration-slice-arm-1-ar-9-cp-0's lifecycle/reviewer correction. If shared-file changes prove necessary, stop for an ordered scope adjustment before writing them. Out: production code, fixtures, goldens, lifecycle/reviewer oracle consumers, other oracle packages, Windows boundary fixes and goal-wide closure.
